title: AI Video Ads: Formats, Examples, and How to Make Them
summary: Learn how AI video ads are made, which formats to use, and how to turn one product into UGC, animated, demo, and social ad creative.
body_markdown:
AI video ads are advertisements created or adapted with artificial intelligence. The AI may research a product page, develop angles, write a script, generate a presenter or visuals, assemble scenes, and resize the result. The strongest workflow is not “press a button and publish.” It is using AI to turn one verified product brief into multiple formats that a marketer reviews and tests.


AI video ads are often treated as a single format. They are not. A creator-style testimonial, an animated product commercial, a software demonstration, and a six-second cutdown can all use AI while looking and behaving completely differently.


That distinction matters. The right question is not merely, “Which AI video generator should I use?” It is, “What does this audience need to see and believe next?”


## The four AI video ad formats marketers actually use


Format Best at Main risk


UGC-style ad Human context, objections, routines, native-feed delivery False or generic testimonial language


Animated or product-motion ad Explaining mechanisms, creating impossible shots, premium visual direction Style without a clear selling idea


Product demo Showing how software or a complex product works Tiny UI, slow pacing, feature overload


Social cutdown Adapting a proven idea to placement and duration Cropping a master without rewriting it


UGC is useful when a human point of view carries the argument. Animation works when the mechanism is difficult to film or the product needs a distinctive visual world. Demos are strongest when seeing the product perform is the proof. Cutdowns let one campaign travel, but only when composition, captions, and pacing are rebuilt for the placement.


The formats can also work together. A UGC presenter can introduce a problem, a screen demonstration can prove the solution, and animation can clarify what is happening behind the scenes.


## What can become an AI video ad?


A useful generation workflow can begin with:


- A product or landing-page URL
- Product photography or existing footage
- App screenshots and screen recordings
- A brand kit, positioning document, or campaign brief
- Approved customer research and product claims
- A script or reference structure


A URL is convenient, but it is not strategy. Product pages commonly omit the audience’s strongest objection, the reason a feature matters, the visual proof an ad needs, or restrictions on what the brand can claim. Treat extracted page content as a starting brief that a person verifies.


## How to turn one product into a campaign


### 1. Verify the source material


Confirm the product name, audience, offer, claims, proof, pricing, visual assets, and prohibited language. Remove old screenshots and unlicensed media. If a claim would require evidence in a traditional ad, AI does not remove that requirement.


### 2. Develop distinct angles


An angle is the argument behind an ad. Useful starting angles include:


- The painful problem the product removes
- The outcome the buyer wants
- A visible product demonstration
- A misunderstood mechanism
- A common objection
- A comparison with the current alternative
- A timely offer or launch


Changing “Stop scrolling” to “Wait” is not a new angle. It is a cosmetic variation.


### 3. Match each angle to a format


Choose UGC when the idea benefits from lived context or a direct explanation. Choose a demo when the interface or product behavior is the evidence. Choose animation or product motion when the benefit is abstract, internal, or visually ambitious.


### 4. Build placement-specific versions


A vertical ad needs a vertical composition, not a center crop. Reposition the product, keep captions out of interface zones, shorten the setup for fast feeds, and make the first frame understandable with sound off. Export horizontal and square versions only when the placement needs them.


### 5. Review before launch


Check product fidelity, spelling, captions, audio, claims, presenter continuity, disclosure requirements, safe zones, and landing-page message match. A realistic render can still be a bad or noncompliant ad.


### 6. Test a hypothesis


Name what each version tests. Hold the audience and offer constant when comparing hooks. Hold the hook and body constant when comparing UGC with animation. A folder of random variations creates volume, not learning.


## What a worked campaign example should document


1. The source page and approved brief.
2. Three distinct angles.
3. One UGC ad, one animated/product-motion ad, one demo, and one cutdown.
4. The exact differences between variants.
5. Generation and review time.
6. Visible limitations or corrections.


The value comes from preserving the decision trail, including limitations and corrections, instead of presenting a polished output without context.
